title: Administration
adminOnly: This page is for system administrators.

placeholder.keyStored: A key is saved — type to change it

users.title: Users

personal.title: Personal data: {{name}}
personal.changeEmailPrompt: New e-mail address for {{name}}. It must not be used by another account.
personal.emailChanged: E-mail address changed. The person's sessions were ended.
personal.emailHelp: Correcting the address ends the person's sessions; they sign in again with the new address. An account that signs in with Google is matched by address, so it then signs in with the Google account of the new address.
personal.exportHelp: A ZIP with the person's profile, company, project memberships and roles, issues and comments, works and correspondence, review steps, audit log rows, outbound log rows, access keys (without their values) and uploaded files, each as JSON and CSV. Prepared in the background; kept for 7 days.
personal.includeFiles: Include the contents of uploaded files
personal.anonymiseHelp: Supports GDPR Art. 17 / KVKK m.7: identifying data is erased and history pseudonymised. Irreversible. The name becomes "Deleted user #…", the e-mail address an invalid one; the password, sessions, access keys, preferences, open invitations and the personal part of the audit and outbound logs are removed. Records the person created stay under the pseudonym; files are not changed. Personal data inside free text (comments, letters) and file contents is not removed automatically. Pseudonymised records remain personal data and are kept only under an Art. 17(3) exception / KVKK m.5(2) condition, then deleted at the end of the retention period.
personal.anonymiseWarning: {{name}}'s identifying data will be erased and their history pseudonymised. This cannot be undone and the account can no longer sign in.
personal.anonymiseType: To confirm, type the account's e-mail address: {{email}}

users.endSessionsConfirm: All browser sessions of {{name}} end. Their API access tokens keep working.
users.resetTwoFactorConfirm: Two-factor authentication of {{name}} is removed and their sessions end. Where it is required, they set it up again at their next sign-in. This is recorded in the audit log.
users.auditorHelp: Read-only auditor: security log, Privacy Centre and every project's audit log; no changes, no files.

companies.title: Companies
companies.help: The short code (2–8 letters/digits) is used in work item numbers (as the sender and recipient code) and as the company code in the new project wizard. If it is empty, the code in the number is derived from the company name. The address and e-mail are suggested as recipient details in formal letters.

googleDomain.title: Allowed Domain
googleDomain.description: When this is on, a person signing in with Google whose domain is in the list and who has no CDE account yet gets a normal user account. They do not become an administrator. A disabled account still cannot sign in.

newUser.title: New User
newUser.capacityWarning: With this addition: {{finding}}. {{action}} Details: System Status → Capacity.

fields.initialPassword: Initial Password (at least 10 characters — the user changes it under My Account)
fields.auditor: Auditor (read-only: security log, Privacy Centre, audit logs)

capacity.title: Capacity
capacity.noTest: No capacity test has been run yet.

test.title: Run Live Test
test.description: The server measures itself; the result shows how many people it can carry and what is missing. Project files are not touched.
test.demoNotice: Sample data: the test engine is still a sample. No load is put on the server; the charts replay a sample run.
test.quickText: Hardware, processor, disk and database speed, a sample IFC conversion, memory headroom.
test.loadText: Virtual users increase step by step; the test stops when the p95 response time exceeds {{p95}} ms, errors exceed {{errorRate}} or the processor exceeds {{cpu}}.
test.loadWarning: Users working during the test may notice slowness. If real user traffic starts, the test stops itself.

run.noLimit: No limit was exceeded up to the top step.
run.firstStepOver: Even the first step was over the limit: {{reason}}.

guide.title: Capacity Guide
guide.intro: Which server is needed for how many users.
guide.estimated: The figures are estimates; they will be updated with a reference measurement.
guide.concurrency: At peak time, {{percent}} of registered users are assumed to work at the same time.
guide.serverSummaryDisk: This server: {{cpu}} vCPU · {{ram}} GB RAM · {{total}} data disk ({{free}} free) · {{os}}.

disk.title: How Disk Is Calculated
disk.description: Disk grows with model volume, not with users: uploaded files × 1.6 (Fragments and previews) + database + 30% free space. Backups are kept on a separate target.

operations.title: How to Run It
operations.whenToTest: Run the capacity test at first installation, when the hardware changes and after a major version upgrade.
operations.oldTest: A test older than {{days}} days shows yellow.
operations.plan: Plan hardware when the number of users reaches 90% of the tier limit; once the limit is exceeded the warning turns red.
operations.afterHours: Run the full load test outside working hours; the Quick Check is always safe.
operations.disk: Extend the disk before it passes 80%.
operations.office: Large IFC conversions and the office server need extra memory; a separate machine is recommended for the office server.

meaning.title: What the Warnings Mean
meaning.ok: The server can handle this number of users.
meaning.warn: The limit is close, the test is old or the disk is filling up. Plan ahead.
meaning.danger: The server cannot handle the number of users. Apply the action shown on screen (RAM, processor, disk).

runs.title: Capacity Reports
runs.empty: No tests yet. Start with Run Live Test.
runs.footnote: Tests are deleted when the server restarts; a permanent report history will come in a later step.

systemStatus.title: System Status
systemStatus.checked: Last check {{time}}. Automatic backup is running; no Grafana or SSH needed.

resources.title: Resources
resources.last24: Last 24 hours. The machine, not project content.

queue.title: Job Queue
queue.description: Conversion, preview and the nightly backup run in this queue.
queue.spark: Waiting, last 24 hours — the queue is draining
queue.dialogDescription: Conversion, preview, clash and backup. A failed job can be queued again.

logs.noDwg: No DWG converter; {{file}} is waiting in the queue

backup.title: Automatic Backup
backup.notScheduled: Scheduling is not on yet. Once the target and the night-time hour are set, the backup job enters the queue.
backup.queued: Backup queued; it finishes in a few minutes.
backup.copiesDescription: Each copy holds the database, the files and the Recovery Package. The latest copy cannot be deleted. Only a system administrator deletes an old copy.
backup.deleteConfirm: Delete the backup of {{date}}? This cannot be undone.

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.cleaned: Derivatives deleted; the files remain. Previews and Fragments are regenerated when first opened.
maintenance.description: Previews and Fragments can be regenerated. Project files and the database are not deleted from here.
maintenance.confirm: Previews and Fragments will be deleted (about {{size}}). Uploaded files and the database stay.

recentErrors.title: Recent Errors
recentErrors.description: Secrets are masked. Not the raw server log; queue and backup lines.
recentErrors.dialogDescription: Keys, sessions and access tokens do not appear in the lines. Project files are not opened.

failedJobs.title: Failed Background Jobs
failedJobs.description: Conversions and synchronisations that did not finish, grouped by job and error. Short network failures are retried automatically (up to 3 runs); what is listed here failed for good.
failedJobs.notRetryable: This kind of job cannot be repeated safely.
failedJobs.retried: {{queued}} queued again, {{skipped}} skipped (already converted, file gone, or not repeatable).
failedJobs.clearConfirm: {{count}} failed job records will be deleted. The files stay as they are. This is recorded in the audit log.

storage.cache: Read cache: {{used}} of {{max}}, {{entries}} files ({{hits}} hits, {{misses}} misses)

kill.title: Turn Off All External Connections
kill.confirmOff: The server's connections to every address outside the network will be cut: cloud AI (including cloud models behind a local server), external e-mail and office servers. AI switches to fully local mode, the external client queue stops, and access keys and connected applications (MCP clients, scripts, OAuth) are suspended until the switch is turned off; nothing is deleted. Browser sign-ins keep working.
kill.confirmOn: External connections will be reopened; each connection returns to its own setting.
kill.on: On. The server connects only to addresses on the local network; AI runs fully locally (cloud models behind a local server stop too), the external client queue has stopped, and access keys and connected applications (MCP, OAuth) are suspended. Browser sign-ins work.
kill.onSince: On ({{date}}). The server connects only to addresses on the local network; AI runs fully locally (cloud models behind a local server stop too), the external client queue has stopped, and access keys and connected applications (MCP, OAuth) are suspended. Browser sign-ins work.
kill.onSinceBy: On ({{date}}, {{name}}). The server connects only to addresses on the local network; AI runs fully locally (cloud models behind a local server stop too), the external client queue has stopped, and access keys and connected applications (MCP, OAuth) are suspended. Browser sign-ins work.
kill.off: Off. When turned on, the server connects to no address outside the network and access keys and connected applications (MCP, OAuth) are suspended; the local network, the internal network list and browser sign-ins keep working.

summary.selectedMode: Selected mode: {{mode}}; running fully locally because external connections are off.
summary.permissionsInvalid: The permissions do not apply right now: the system mode does not allow external providers.

settings.title: Settings

options.redactLocal: Mask for the Local Model Too

settings.redactLocalHint: (personal data goes to the local model with placeholders too)
settings.redactNamesHint: (role and company are sent instead of the name, e.g. "Project Manager (Poyraz)")
settings.always: In every prompt to AI outside the network, e-mail addresses, phone numbers, Turkish ID numbers and IBANs are always replaced with placeholders. The originals are put back when the answer is shown to you; the mapping is kept in memory only for that call.
settings.lanHelp: Servers that are on your network even though their names look public (one name per line, "*.domain" or an IPv4 range). Private IP ranges and single-label names are already local. The entries in this list count as local: they keep working while all external connections are off, and AI prompts to them are not masked.
settings.auditRetentionHelp: IP addresses, browser details and e-mail addresses in the audit log are deleted once this period has passed ({{min}}–{{max}} months). The entries themselves stay, and the chain check still passes.

location.localHint: Inside your network (private IP range or internal network list)
location.inboundHint: External clients connect to the CDE; the server does not connect out

connections.stoppedHint: Does not work while external connections are off.

log.description: The time, purpose, server, size and result of every external call are kept; the content never is. Entries are deleted every day once the retention period has passed.
log.empty: No entries. The server made no external connection matching this filter.

retention.title: Retention periods
retention.intro: A daily job deletes what is older than these periods and writes the counts to the audit log and the disposal record.

fields.trash: Recycle bin: delete for good after

retention.trashHelp: Files and folders deleted longer ago than this are deleted for good, with their versions and stored contents. Items still used elsewhere (e.g. in a review) stay.
retention.auditLogHelp: At least {{min}} year (ISO 19650 and contracts usually require the whole project). Older rows are deleted with a checkpoint, so the chain check still passes.

always.outbound: Outbound connection log rows after {{days}} days (Summary → Settings)
always.auditPersonal: IP address, user agent and e-mail in the audit log after {{months}} months (Summary → Settings)
always.credentials: Expired sessions, API keys and OAuth tokens and codes
always.invitations: Invitations not accepted, 30 days after they expired or were revoked
always.exports: Personal data exports, 7 days after they were prepared

retention.disposalHelp: What the daily job deleted, by category, with counts and the time span of the deleted records (never the records themselves). Basis for the periodic destruction report (KVKK).

notice.title: Privacy Notice
notice.intro: Text shown on the sign-in page and on the invitation page, for example the privacy notice your organisation gives as data controller (GDPR Art. 13, KVKK m.10). Write it in English and Turkish; each page shows the language the person chose, or the other one when that is empty.

fields.enabled: Show on the Sign-in and Invitation Pages
fields.requireAck: Require “I Have Read the Privacy Notice” Before Sign-in
fields.reask: Ask Again When the Text Changes

notice.markupHelp: Light markup: blank line between paragraphs, # heading, - list item, **bold**, *italic*, [link](https://…). HTML is shown as text.
notice.version: Version {{version}}, saved {{date}} by {{name}}. Accepted by {{count}} people.
notice.newVersion: Saving the changed text makes a new version. Its text is written to the audit log.
notice.newVersionReask: Saving the changed text makes a new version; everyone accepts it again at their next sign-in. Its text is written to the audit log.

mode.title: AI Mode
mode.killSwitch: All external connections are off (Privacy Centre): AI runs fully locally and the external client queue has stopped. The mode you choose applies once connections are reopened.
mode.projectsLimit: Projects cannot go beyond this limit: the project administrator can turn AI off under Project Settings → AI, or choose only providers the system mode allows. External models work only in projects that allow them.
mode.order: Order: local model → cloud model → "Run with My Own AI" (fallback). The options can be combined.

options.allowWrite: Allow Read + Write Access Tokens (needed for the task queue and the saving tools)

editorTexts.none: Office files open only in the browser viewers; to edit, they are downloaded and uploaded again.
editorTexts.onlyoffice: AGPL-3.0. The editor most faithful to Microsoft formats (docx/xlsx/pptx). The free edition allows at most 20 concurrent connections. Needs WOPI_ENABLED=true and JWT.
editorTexts.collabora: MPL-2.0, based on LibreOffice. Strong with ODF and older formats (doc/xls/ppt). The CODE edition has no connection limit but shows a warning as load grows.

converterTexts.auto: The editor's server if an editor is set up; otherwise LibreOffice on this server if present; otherwise no PDF is made (files still open in the browser).
converterTexts.onlyoffice: ConvertService API (JWT). ONLYOFFICE downloads the file from the CDE through a single-use address.
converterTexts.collabora: /cool/convert-to/pdf. Collabora must allow the CDE server (net.post_allow).
converterTexts.gotenberg: MIT-licensed lightweight conversion service with LibreOffice (/forms/libreoffice/convert). It only converts; it does not edit.
converterTexts.local: soffice installed on this server. A last resort; no longer in the Docker image.
converterTexts.none: Conversion is off. Office files get no PDF view, markup or visual comparison.

overview.title: Status
overview.testHint: Tries the editor and the converter with the saved settings
overview.fromEnv: Defaults from environment variables: {{vars}}. A value saved here takes precedence.

wopi.title: Browser Editing (WOPI)

fields.editorUrl: Editor Address (as reached by the CDE server)
fields.publicUrl: Address Used by the Browser (if different)
fields.wopiBase: The CDE Address as Seen by the Editor

placeholder.publicUrl: e.g. https://office.company.com — if empty, the address the editor reports

options.verifyProof: Verify the Signature of WOPI Requests (X-WOPI-Proof, with the editor's discovery key). Do not turn this off except while troubleshooting.

wopi.help: The editor reads the file from here and saves it here (e.g. http://app:8080 on a Docker network). ONLYOFFICE conversion uses this address too.

converter.title: Office → PDF Converter
converter.description: For the PDF view of office files, markup, visual revision comparison and batch PDF. Files are sent only to the address set here.

connection.title: Connection Details
connection.description: OpenCDE clients (Solibri, IfcOpenShell, BCF tools) first ask for the server address; they find the other addresses themselves through /foundation/versions and /foundation/1.1/auth. Some forms ask for each one separately.
connection.notConfigured: These addresses were derived from the address of the request. On the server, set the CDE_PUBLIC_URL variable to the HTTPS address the customer uses (e.g. https://cde.company.local).

oauth.secretNotice: Copy the secret for "{{name}}" now; it will not be shown again:

apps.title: OAuth Applications
apps.aecPilotHint: Ready-made entry for the Revit / Civil 3D add-in: public client, local redirect, OpenCDE Documents permission
apps.description: Applications connect with the user's consent and with the user's own project and folder permissions. The user can remove access under My Account → Connected Applications.
apps.rotateConfirm: Generate a new secret for "{{name}}"? The old secret stops working immediately.
apps.deleteConfirm: Delete "{{name}}"? All users' consents and access tokens are deleted too.

info.title: {{name}}: Connection Details
info.description: The Solibri private connection form and other OpenCDE clients ask for these values.
info.secretHint: The secret is shown only when it is created; if it is lost, regenerate it.

dialog.redirectHelp: Addresses must match exactly. For desktop applications, http://127.0.0.1 and http://localhost match any port. Other addresses must use https.
dialog.scopesHelp: Read and Write open the existing SiteKeep API. The BCF and Documents permissions are for the OpenCDE APIs.

forma.title: Forma Sync
forma.description: Autodesk ACC / Forma folders and files. Records (issues, reviews) sync separately; the file engine does not exist yet — this screen is a sample.

syncNow.title: Sync Now
syncNow.confirm: The file sync will look as if it was queued. The engine does not exist yet; no files come down from ACC.

connection.hint: Connect an ACC project under Project Settings → Autodesk.

recent.title: Recently Transferred
recent.description: Names that do not match are skipped; files deleted at the source stay in the CDE. Once the engine is connected this list becomes `integration_sync_runs`.

addDialog.title: Add Mapping
addDialog.hint: Not saved. Once Data Management is connected, it is chosen from the folder tree.

license.title: Licence

statusText.none: SiteKeep Community: the core is free and not limited. Install a licence to turn on Enterprise modules.
statusText.not_yet: The licence starts on its validity date; until then Enterprise modules stay off.
statusText.expiring: The licence ends in {{days}} days. Renew it to keep the Enterprise modules.
statusText.grace: The licence has ended. Enterprise modules become read-only on {{date}} unless it is renewed.
statusText.read_only: The licence has ended: Enterprise modules are read-only until it is renewed. The core is not affected.
statusText.invalid: The licence file cannot be used.

license.notEnforced: Licence checks are off on this installation (SITEKEEP_LICENSE_ENFORCE): modules follow the installed packages.
license.clockBehind: The server clock is behind the latest time seen; the licence is judged by that time.
license.installationText: Send this id when you ask for a licence; the licence is made for this installation.
license.uploadText: Choose the licence file (license.json) you received.
license.removeText: Enterprise modules turn off; their data stays and comes back with a licence.

problems.format: This is not a SiteKeep licence file.
problems.unknown_key: The licence was signed with a key this version does not know.
problems.dev_key_in_production: This is a development licence; it does not work on a production installation.
problems.signature: The licence signature does not match: the file was changed or damaged.
problems.payload: The licence content cannot be read.
problems.other_installation: This licence belongs to another installation.
problems.build_after_support: This SiteKeep version was released after the support period ended.

license.seatsOver: {{count}} more active users than the licence allows: Enterprise modules are read-only until accounts are disabled or seats are added.

online.onlineText: Enter the activation key you received (SK-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX). The server fetches the licence and renews it every night; it sends only the installation id, the version and the number of active users.
online.trialText: Plus modules for 10 users, once per installation.
online.lastOk: Last answer from the licensing service: {{date}}
online.offlineHint: No internet on this server? Upload the licence file from the customer portal below instead.

onlineProblems.revoked: The licensing service no longer accepts this licence ({{reason}}): Enterprise modules turn read-only on {{date}} unless it is resolved.
onlineProblems.offline_too_long: This licence must be checked online, and the licensing service has not been reached for more than 30 days: Enterprise modules turn read-only on {{date}}.

invitations.title: Invitations
invitations.description: People without an account can be invited to a project by e-mail (Project Settings → Members and the set-up wizard). System administrators can always invite. Off by default: project administrators can only add people who already have an account.
invitations.projectAdmins: Project Administrators May Invite People Without an Account

security.title: Sign-in Security
security.description: Limits for failed sign-ins, session lifetimes and two-factor authentication. Changes are recorded in the audit log.

twoFactor.heading: Two-factor authentication
twoFactor.help: People it covers who have not set it up yet do so at their next sign-in, before their session starts. Sessions already open continue. API access tokens and OAuth applications are not affected.

help.failureLimit: Then the account is locked until the oldest failure leaves the window (default 10).
help.ipFailureLimit: Across all accounts; a whole office may share one address (default 50).
help.failureWindowMinutes: Failures older than this no longer count (default 15).
help.sessionAbsoluteDays: A session ends this long after sign-in, however active (default 14).
help.sessionIdleHours: A session ends after this long without use; 0 turns it off (default 12).

unlock.heading: Locked sign-ins
unlock.description: Lift every current lock now, for example after a person mistyped their password too often.

auditor.notice: You are signed in as an auditor: you can read the security log, the audit log of every project and the Privacy Centre, and download them as CSV. You cannot change anything.

securityLog.title: Security Log
securityLog.description: Sign-ins and failed sign-ins, lockouts, two-factor changes, users and their rights, permission and settings changes, external connections, access keys and OAuth grants, exports of the logs and security alerts, across every project and outside projects, newest first. The IP address and browser are shown while they are kept (Privacy Centre → Retention).
securityLog.allDescription: The audit log of every project and of the system, newest first.

securityAlerts.notification: If an alert may be a personal data breach, the GDPR (Art. 33) requires notifying the supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, and the KVKK (Art. 12) requires notifying the Board as soon as possible. Acknowledging or dismissing an alert is recorded in the audit log.

failed_sign_ins_account.title: Many Failed Sign-Ins for One Account
failed_sign_ins_account.body: {{count}} failed sign-ins for one account within {{minutes}} minutes (threshold {{threshold}}).

failed_sign_ins_global.title: Many Failed Sign-Ins
failed_sign_ins_global.body: {{count}} failed sign-ins on the installation within {{minutes}} minutes (threshold {{threshold}}).

bulk_download.title: Bulk Download
bulk_download.body: One person downloaded {{count}} files within {{minutes}} minutes (threshold {{threshold}}).

new_admin.title: New System Administrator
new_admin.body: A user was given System Administrator rights.

kill_switch_off.title: External Connections Turned On Again
kill_switch_off.body: "Turn Off All External Connections" was switched off: external connections are allowed again.

two_factor_off.title: Two-Factor Requirement Turned Off
two_factor_off.body: Two-factor authentication is no longer required at sign-in.

audit_chain_broken.title: Audit Chain Check Failed
audit_chain_broken.body: The daily check of the audit log's hash chain failed at entry {{id}} ({{reason}}).

settings.title: Security Alerts
settings.description: Alerts appear as cards at the top of the Administration page until a system administrator acknowledges or dismisses them. The audit log is checked every minute and the hash chain once a day. Changes are recorded in the audit log.
settings.emailHelp: One address per line, at most 10. The e-mail names the alert and its time only, no personal data.

mail.smtp_not_configured: No e-mail is sent: SMTP is not configured (CDE_SMTP_URL, CDE_SMTP_FROM).
mail.smtp_disabled: No e-mail is sent: SMTP is switched off in the Privacy Centre.

oidc.title: OpenID Connect Sign-in
oidc.description: Sign-in with your organisation's identity provider (Entra ID, Keycloak, Okta, Google Workspace, Authentik …). Each provider gets a button on the sign-in page and its own switch in the Privacy Centre. Changes are recorded in the audit log.
oidc.deleteConfirm: Delete {{name}}? Its sign-in button disappears; the accounts stay.
oidc.secretStored: Stored — leave empty to keep it

fields.name: Display Name
fields.redirectUri: Redirect URI (register it at the provider)

help.id: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens; used in the redirect URI and cannot be changed later.
help.issuer: SiteKeep reads the issuer URL followed by /.well-known/openid-configuration. https:// is required (http:// only for localhost).
help.redirectUri: After saving, the redirect URI to register at the provider is shown here.
help.allowedDomains: Separated by commas; subdomains match. Empty: any domain.
help.createAccounts: Off (recommended): only existing users and people with an open invitation can sign in. On: a new person becomes a normal user.
help.adminGroup: When set, members of this group (in the groups claim) become system administrators at sign-in. It is never taken away automatically.
help.trustUnverifiedEmail: Off: the address must be verified by the provider (email_verified). Turn on only for a provider whose addresses the organisation itself assigns.
help.trustProviderMfa: On: when the provider reports a multi-factor sign-in (amr), SiteKeep does not ask for its own two-factor code. Off: two-factor applies as after a password.

updates.title: New Versions
updates.automaticLabel: Check for new versions once a day
updates.privacy: Once a day SiteKeep asks GitHub for the latest release number. Nothing about your installation is sent. Administration → Privacy Centre lists and can stop this connection.
updates.devBuild: This is a development build, so no update is offered.

prompt.title: Check for new versions automatically?
prompt.text: Once a day SiteKeep asks GitHub for the latest release number; nothing about your installation is sent. You can turn it off any time.

available.title: SiteKeep {{latest}} is available — you have {{current}}
available.compose: Docker Compose: set the new version in .env, then
available.backup: Take a backup before updating; database migrations run automatically at startup.
